title: Bettendorf honors 7 police officers for bravery, service - NewsBreak
text:
By Sharon Wren ,
11 hours ago
Seven members of the Bettendorf Police Department (BPD) were honored for their dedication, bravery and exemplary service. Chief Doug Scott presented awards for Combat Cross, Wounded in Combat, Honorable Service and Community Service to these officers on October 7:
Officers Landry Blunk and Brian Morrisey – Combat Cross/Wounded in Combat
Officers Landry Blunk and Brian Morrisey (City of Bettendorf) On May 21, 2025, at about 1:26 a.m., officers were dispatched to the 2600 block of Cypress Drive for a report of a domestic disturbance involving a stabbing. Officers Blunk and Morrisey arrived on the scene and Officer Blunk encountered a child in the front doorway and two other children inside the residence. They successfully evacuated all three of the children to safety. Officer Blunk was securing the children when he heard shouting and the sound of a firearm slide being racked in the basement. Officer Blunk was informed about several occupants and a prior stabbing. He opened the basement door and saw a person holding a handgun. The person turned, raised the firearm and fired two rounds, striking Officer Blunk in the forearm and hip. Officer Blunk returned fire, striking the person, who dropped the firearm. One round that struck Officer Blunk also struck Officer Morrisey in the thumb. Officer Blunk exited the residence, administered self-aid and stayed on scene to direct responding officers. Officer Morrisey, despite injury to his dominant hand, covered the threat area with his support hand until additional officers arrived.
Reinforcements secured the scene while Officer Morrisey checked Officer Blunk for injuries and took both officers to the hospital for treatment.
Lieutenant Zach Thomas – Combat Cross
Lieutenant Zach Thomas (City of Bettendorf) On October 30, 2022, at about 2:50 a.m., several law enforcement agencies were conducting patrols near 5200 Grand Avenue in Davenport. Officers initiated a traffic stop on a vehicle, but it failed to stop and led to a pursuit. The pursuit ended when the vehicle crashed near the intersection of Kimberly Road and Elmore Avenue. Then – Bettendorf Police Sergeant Zach Thomas (promoted to Lieutenant in June 2025) responded to the scene. The vehicle’s occupants fled on foot and during the foot pursuit, one of the people discharged several rounds from his firearm toward responding officers. Sergeant Thomas, along with five other officers, fired their firearms, striking the suspect.
Officer Derrick Said – Honorable Service
Officer Derrick Said (City of Bettendorf) On June 26, 2025, at about 12:56 a.m., Officer Derrick Said responded to a call on the I-74 Bridge about a suicidal woman who was threatening to jump. Officer Said arrived in the area and began searching for the woman. He found her and noticed that she was in significant distress, having climbed over the railing and clinging to a light post. Officer Said remained calm and maintained continuous, highly effective communication with the woman while working with other officers on scene to establish potential life-saving measures. Through his interventions, and with the assistance of fellow officers, Officer Said was able to convince the woman to accept help and safely return over the railing.
Officer Herve Denain – Honorable Service
Officer Herve Denain (City of Bettendorf) On February 19, 2025 at about 5:29 p.m., Officer Herve Denain was on a routine patrol in the Wilderness Pointe area near Criswell Street in Bettendorf when the Scott Emergency Communication Center received a medical call for a man down at a nearby address. The call originated from the Scott County Sheriff’s Department. The homeowner reported that a relative had collapsed while skating on a pond in the backyard. Officer Denain was the closest law enforcement unit and responded to the scene. The person collapsed in a place that was over 100 yards from the home and the ambient temperature at the time was 7 degrees Fahrenheit. Officer Denain found the man in the backyard and immediately assumed CPR compressions from the homeowner, who was exhausted from performing resuscitation efforts. The man was later successfully revived by fire personnel.
Officer Ashley Guffey & Records Specialist Sara Stolley (not pictured) – Community Service
Pink Patch Project
(Bettendorf Police Department) In 2018, Officers Ashley Guffey and Sara Stolley launched the Social Awareness Patch Program in partnership with the Pink Patch Project . The program’s success has generated a significant impact on both the police department and the community. The program has expanded to include campaigns promoting Mental Health and Suicide Prevention, Autism Awareness and Heart Health. The program has expanded to include merchandise sales. All proceeds generated through these initiatives are donated to local organizations that work to improve the lives of Quad City residents.
(City of Bettendorf) “I am incredibly proud of our officers whose daily acts of selflessness, empathy, and courage exemplify the very best of public service,” said Chief Scott.
“It is very gratifying to celebrate the outstanding heroism, dedication, talent, and service of these seven officers who make our city stronger and safer,” said Mayor Bob Gallagher. “Please help me honor those who go above and beyond for our community.”
